title: New in ctsem 4
text: Random effects integrated Laplace approximation. Version 3 carried extra states Kalman filter, underestimates individual differences dynamics. linear models, random intercepts integrated exactly. intoverpop = 'augmented' gives old method, ctFit() warns method meets nonlinear dynamics. fit checks approximation warns affects estimates. intoverpop = 'quadrature' refines fit, ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample') samples full posterior instead. Random effects can multiple nested levels, people within couples: id = c('person', 'couple'), parameter’s indvarying naming levels varies . See multilevel vignette. poprank, popunique popblocks give random effects covariance fewer parameters many parameters vary.

code: library(ctsem) library(ggplot2)  set.seed(49)  n_subjects <- 20 n_obs <- 80  raw_param_names <- c("t0m", "drift", "diffusion", "mmean") raw_cor <- matrix(c(    1.00,  0.45, -0.25,  0.35,    0.45,  1.00, -0.55,  0.25,   -0.25, -0.55,  1.00, -0.20,    0.35,  0.25, -0.20,  1.00 ), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(raw_param_names, raw_param_names)) raw_sd <- c(t0m = .7, drift = .55, diffusion = .35, mmean = 2.45) raw_mean <- c(t0m = 0, drift = -.4, diffusion = log(exp(.45) - 1), mmean = 0) raw_cov <- diag(raw_sd) %*% raw_cor %*% diag(raw_sd) dimnames(raw_cov) <- dimnames(raw_cor)  # Each subject's raw parameters are drawn from this population by ctGenerate: # RAWPOPVAR is the covariance of the raw (pre-transform) parameters, written # from a covariance matrix by ctCov(), and values the population means on # the natural scale. gm <- ctModel(   silent = TRUE,   Tpoints = n_obs,   latentNames = "eta",   manifestNames = "Y",   LAMBDA = matrix(1),   T0MEANS = matrix("t0m|param|TRUE"),   DRIFT = matrix("drift|-log1p_exp(-param)|TRUE"),   DIFFUSION = matrix("diffusion|log1p_exp(param)|TRUE"),   CINT = matrix(0),   T0VAR = matrix(0),   MANIFESTMEANS = matrix("mmean|param|TRUE"),   MANIFESTVAR = matrix(.35) ) gm$RAWPOPVAR <- ctCov(raw_cov) softplus <- function(x) ifelse(x > 30, x, log1p(exp(x)))  generated <- ctGenerate(gm, n = n_subjects, dtmean = .1, backend = "julia",   values = c(t0m = raw_mean[["t0m"]], drift = -softplus(-raw_mean[["drift"]]),     diffusion = softplus(raw_mean[["diffusion"]]), mmean = raw_mean[["mmean"]]))  # The parameters each subject was generated with, on the natural scale, and # back on the raw scale through the inverse transforms. truth <- attr(generated, "subjectpars")[, c("id", raw_param_names)] raw_truth <- data.frame(id = truth$id, t0m = truth$t0m,   drift = -log(expm1(-truth$drift)), diffusion = log(expm1(truth$diffusion)),   mmean = truth$mmean)  dat <- data.frame(generated)[, c("id", "time", "Y")] ggplot(dat[dat$id <= 4, ], aes(time, Y, group = id, colour = factor(id))) +   geom_line(linewidth = .35) + theme_bw()+   labs(colour = "subject")

text: ctEmpiricalBayesFit() uses two subject-wise passes default. First, fits model per subject using model prior. raw estimates first-pass fits define marginal empirical Bayes prior. Second, rewrites single-subject model transforms raw normal(0, 1) parameters imply empirical location scale, fits every subject . final $fits element contains final EB-prior fits; $initialfits contains model-prior fits, $passfits contains every pass. transform adjustment unconstrained raw scale. original model transforms raw parameter qq model parameter θ\theta θ=f(q),\theta = f(q), EB-adjusted model uses new local raw parameter z∼N(0,1)z \sim N(0, 1) sets θ=f(μq+σqz),\theta = f(\mu_q + \sigma_q z), μq\mu_q σq\sigma_q empirical mean standard deviation subject-level raw estimates. example, positive parameter log1p_exp(param) becomes log1p_exp(mu + sigma * param). Npasses > 2, later pass maps local EB raw estimates back original raw scale recomputing μq\mu_q σq\sigma_q. gives iterated marginal EB prior, still encode empirical covariance among raw parameters. default, EB prior construction robust extreme first-pass raw estimates: raw values winsorized using quantile MAD bounds, prior location scale computed median MAD. protects second pass single subject fit unusual optimum. Set ebRobust = FALSE, adjust ebOutlierQuantiles, ebOutlierMAD, ebWinsorize, want different behavior. optimized fits, first pass uses optimcontrol$estonly = TRUE, point estimates needed build EB prior. stochastic optimizer disabled default passes; pass optimcontrol = list(stochastic = TRUE) want override . summary transformed parameter scale, matching scale users usually inspect summary(ctFit(...)). code: DRIFT <- matrix(c(-0.5, 0,                   0.3, -0.5), 2, 2, byrow = TRUE)   # eta1 -> eta2 is 0.3 diffsd <- 2.2 diffcor <- 0.4 thresholds <- c(-2.8, -1.0, 1.0, 2.8)  # covmattransform='z' makes a covariance matrix's off-diagonal exactly # atanh(correlation), so the generating values can be written down. zmat <- function(sd1, sd2, r) matrix(c(sd1, 0, atanh(r), sd2), 2, 2, byrow = TRUE)  # Stationary covariance, solving A S + S A' + Q = 0: its standard deviations # are what the true standardised cross effect is scaled by. Q <- diag(diffsd, 2) %*% matrix(c(1, diffcor, diffcor, 1), 2) %*% diag(diffsd, 2) S <- matrix(solve(kronecker(diag(2), DRIFT) + kronecker(DRIFT, diag(2)),   -as.vector(Q)), 2, 2) latentsd <- sqrt(diag(S))  gen <- ctModel(type = 'ct', n.latent = 2, n.manifest = 2,   manifestNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'), latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'),   LAMBDA = diag(1, 2), DRIFT = DRIFT,   DIFFUSION = zmat(diffsd, diffsd, diffcor),   T0VAR = diag(1,2),   T0MEANS = matrix(1, 2, 1), CINT = matrix(0, 2, 1),   MANIFESTMEANS = matrix(0, 2, 1),   MANIFESTVAR = diag(1e-6, 2),          # no measurement error: manifest = state   Tpoints = 30) gen$covmattransform <- 'z'  # backend='julia' because the R generator reads DIFFUSION and T0VAR as square # roots whatever covmattransform says, while the julia generator applies the # declared transform, as ctFit() does. set.seed(2) d <- data.frame(ctGenerate(gen, n = 150, Tpoints = 30, dtmean = 0.7,   backend = 'julia'))  # The cumulative logit: the response falls in category k or below when the # state plus a logistic disturbance is below threshold k. ordinalise <- function(eta)   1 + rowSums(outer(eta + rlogis(length(eta)), thresholds, '>')) # Moderate individual differences: each person's process sits a little high or # low. Added to the states, before they are categorised. set.seed(3) shift <- matrix(stats::rnorm(150 * 2, 0, 0.8), 150, 2) d$eta1 <- d$eta1 + shift[d$id, 1] d$eta2 <- d$eta2 + shift[d$id, 2]  set.seed(502) d$y1 <- ordinalise(d$eta1) d$y2 <- ordinalise(d$eta2) mid <- c(-3.8, -1.9, 0, 1.9, 3.8)             # band midpoints, for display s <- d[d$id == 1, ]  ggplot(s, aes(time)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = thresholds, linetype = 3, colour = 'grey55') +   geom_line(aes(y = eta1, colour = 'latent eta1')) +   geom_point(aes(y = mid[y1], colour = 'recorded category y1'), size = 1.9) +   scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~., breaks = mid, labels = 1:5,     name = 'category')) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c('latent eta1' = 'grey35',     'recorded category y1' = '#c0392b')) +   theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = 'bottom') +   labs(x = 'time', y = 'latent scale', colour = NULL) freq <- rbind(data.frame(item = 'y1', category = factor(d$y1)),   data.frame(item = 'y2', category = factor(d$y2)))  ggplot(freq, aes(category)) + geom_bar() + facet_wrap(~item) +   theme_bw() + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)

TDpredNames='TD1',   TIpredNames=c('TI1','TI2','TI3'),   LAMBDA=diag(2))  # The default backend is julia; ctJuliaInstall() sets it up. if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {   fit<-ctFit(ctstantestdat, model,priors=TRUE)    summary(fit)    plot(fit,wait=FALSE) }  #### extended examples  library(ctsem) set.seed(3)  #  Data generation (run this, but no need to understand!) -----------------  Tpoints <- 20 nmanifest <- 4 nlatent <- 2 nsubjects<-20  #random effects age <- rnorm(nsubjects) #standardised cint1<-rnorm(nsubjects,2,.3)+age*.5 cint2 <- cint1*.5+rnorm(nsubjects,1,.2)+age*.5 tdpredeffect <- rnorm(nsubjects,5,.3)+age*.5  for(i in 1:nsubjects){   #generating model   gm<-ctModel(Tpoints=Tpoints,n.manifest = nmanifest,n.latent = nlatent,n.TDpred = 1,   type='omx',     LAMBDA = matrix(c(1,0,0,0, 0,1,.8,1.3),nrow=nmanifest,ncol=nlatent),     DRIFT=matrix(c(-.3, .2, 0, -.5),nlatent,nlatent),     TDPREDMEANS=matrix(c(rep(0,Tpoints-10),1,rep(0,9)),ncol=1),     TDPREDEFFECT=matrix(c(tdpredeffect[i],0),nrow=nlatent),     DIFFUSION = matrix(c(1, 0, 0, .5),2,2),     CINT = matrix(c(cint1[i],cint2[i]),ncol=1),     T0VAR=diag(2,nlatent,nlatent),     MANIFESTVAR = diag(.5, nmanifest))    #generate data   newdat <- ctGenerate(ctmodelobj = gm,n = 1,burnin = 2,     dtmat=rbind(c(rep(.5,8),3,rep(.5,Tpoints-9))))   newdat[,'id'] <- i #set id for each subject   newdat <- cbind(newdat,age[i]) #include time independent predictor   if(i ==1) {     dat <- newdat[1:(Tpoints-10),] #pre intervention data     dat2 <- newdat #including post intervention data   }   if(i > 1) {     dat <- rbind(dat, newdat[1:(Tpoints-10),])     dat2 <- rbind(dat2,newdat)   } } colnames(dat)[ncol(dat)] <- 'age' colnames(dat2)[ncol(dat)] <- 'age'   #plot generated data for sanity plot(age) matplot(dat[,gm$manifestNames],type='l',pch=1) plotvar <- 'Y1' plot(dat[dat[,'id']==1,'time'],dat[dat[,'id']==1,plotvar],type='l',   ylim=range(dat[,plotvar],na.rm=TRUE)) for(i in 2:nsubjects){   points(dat[dat[,'id']==i,'time'],dat[dat[,'id']==i,plotvar],type='l',col=i) }   dat2[,gm$manifestNames][sample(1:length(dat2[,gm$manifestNames]),size = 100)] <- NA   #data structure head(dat2)   # Model fitting -----------------------------------------------------------  ##simple univariate default model  m <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = c('Y1'), LAMBDA = diag(1)) ctModelLatex(m)  #Specify univariate linear growth curve  m1 <- ctModel(type = 'ct',   manifestNames = c('Y1'), latentNames=c('eta1'),   DRIFT=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=1),   DIFFUSION=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=1),   T0VAR=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=1),   CINT=matrix(c('cint1'),ncol=1),   T0MEANS=matrix(c('t0m1'),ncol=1),   LAMBDA = diag(1),   MANIFESTMEANS=matrix(0,ncol=1),   MANIFESTVAR=matrix(c('merror'),nrow=1,ncol=1))  ctModelLatex(m1)  #fit if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {   f1 <- ctFit(datalong = dat2, model = m1, optimize=TRUE, priors=FALSE)    summary(f1)    #plots of individual subject models v data   ctPredict(f1,plot=TRUE,subjects=1,kalmanvec=c('y','yprior'),timestep=.01)   ctPredict(f1,plot=TRUE,subjects=1:3,kalmanvec=c('y','ysmooth'),timestep=.01,errorvec=NA)    #compare randomly generated data from the posterior to the observed data,   #including the lagged covariance structure and the mean trajectory over time   ctPostPredict(f1, wait=FALSE) }   ### Further example models  #Include intervention m2 <- ctModel(type = 'ct',   manifestNames = c('Y1'), latentNames=c('eta1'),   n.TDpred=1,TDpredNames = 'TD1', #this line includes the intervention   TDPREDEFFECT=matrix(c('tdpredeffect'),nrow=1,ncol=1), #intervention effect   DRIFT=matrix(-1e-5,nrow=1,ncol=1),   DIFFUSION=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=1),   CINT=matrix(c('cint1'),ncol=1),   T0MEANS=matrix(c('t0m1'),ncol=1),   T0VAR=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=1),   LAMBDA = diag(1),   MANIFESTMEANS=matrix(0,ncol=1),   MANIFESTVAR=matrix(c('merror'),nrow=1,ncol=1))    #Individual differences in intervention, Bayesian estimation, covariates m2i <- ctModel(type = 'ct',   manifestNames title: Visual lagged covariance or correlation diagnostics for ctsem fits. — ctFitCheckCov
code: # \donttest{ # Lagged correlations for all manifest variables, lags 0 to 3. ctFitCheckCov(ctstantestfit, cor = TRUE, lags = 0:3, plot = TRUE)  # Lagged covariances for one manifest variable. ctFitCheckCov(ctstantestfit, cor = FALSE, variables = "Y1", lags = 0:5,   plot = FALSE)  # Variances, covariances and lag-1 covariances at each wave rather than # averaged over waves, and the same by bins of time. ctFitCheckCov(ctstantestfit, cor = FALSE, x = "obs") ctFitCheckCov(ctstantestfit, cor = FALSE, x = "time", xbins = 5)  # Lag each variable by its own previous observation, for variables # measured at only some waves. ctFitCheckCov(ctstantestfit, x = "obs", lagrows = "observed")  # Split the diagnostic by a time independent predictor in the fitted data. gg <- ctFitCheckCov(ctstantestfit, cor = TRUE, splitby = "TI1", lags = 0:3) print(gg[[1]])  # Use an external subject-level variable for the split. splitdat <- unique(data.frame(ctstantestdat)[, "id", drop = FALSE]) splitdat$group <- rep(c("a", "b"), length.out = nrow(splitdat)) ctFitCheckCov(ctstantestfit, splitby = "group", splitdata = splitdat,   lags = 0:2)  # Split observations into early and late periods within each subject. dat <- data.table::as.data.table(data.frame(ctstantestdat)) dat[, period := ifelse(time <= stats::median(time, na.rm = TRUE),   "early", "late"), by = id] ctFitCheckCov(ctstantestfit, data = dat, splitby = "period",   split = "factor", lags = 0:2) # }

code: # \donttest{ # Needs a working julia backend, so the example is inert where Julia is # absent -- including on CRAN, whose check machines have none. if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {   model <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = 'Y1', latentNames = 'eta1',     LAMBDA = matrix(1))   model$pars$indvarying <- FALSE   fit <- ctFit(ctstantestdat, model, backend = 'julia', cores = 1)    # Two named parameters; parameters = "flagged" profiles only those the   # fit's own diagnostics doubt, and NULL profiles every one.   result <- ctFitProfile(fit, parameters = c('drift_eta1', 'mm_Y1'))   print(result)   plot(result)   # Julia keeps running between calls, holding what it has compiled;   # this ends it.   ctJuliaKill("session") } # }

title: ctsem 4.0.0
text: 14/10/2026 major release. ctsem second estimation engine, written Julia, new features need now default ctFit(). Use backend='stan' previous behaviour. New backend='julia' ctFit(), exact gradients Hessians, using multiple cores. ctJuliaInstall() installs Julia engine, asking download, ctJuliaStatus(), ctJuliaSetup(), ctJuliaProcesses() ctJuliaKill() manage Julia sessions. Random effects parameter, including variances, nonlinear dynamics non-Gaussian indicators, integrated Laplace approximation (intoverpop='laplace', default optimising). fit checks approximation, intoverpop='quadrature' refines fit needed. Julia backend . Nested grouping levels, id=c('person','couple'). parameter’s indvarying names levels varies , poprank can set per level. Julia backend . Ordinal, count censored indicators, lower upper asymptotes binary indicators (ASYMPTOTES ctModel()). Julia backend . Posterior sampling ctFit(backend='julia', optimize=FALSE), ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample') optimised fit. Sampling continues target effective sample size reached. Smooth effects time independent predictors, ctModel(TIpredNames = ~ s(age) + sex), smoothness estimated data. ctTIpredEffects(fit, whichTIpreds = 'age') shows estimated effect. Julia backend . Sampling weights, one per subject, ctFit(weights=). Fits maximise weighted pseudo-likelihood report robust standard errors. See sampling weights vignette. Julia backend . ctOptimUncertainty() renamed ctFitUncertainty(), old name still works. New methods include 'sample', 'stored' draw covariance stored fit, importance sampling quadrature particle filter likelihood (intoverpop='quadrature', filter='particle'). New uncertainty='checked', checks Hessian’s normal approximation uses importance sampling hold. uncertainty='surrogate' removed. Use 'checked' instead. julia backend, missing values time independent predictors imputed optimising sampled sampling, nlcontrol$nsubsteps='auto' chooses number integration steps nonlinear model. ctFit(stationary=TRUE) works , backend='julia'. Model matrix cells accept named form, 'mm, indvarying=TRUE, sdscale=0.5', well 'mm||TRUE|0.5'. ctPar() writes either form, ctCov() writes covariance matrix cells. Covariance matrices parameterised matrix logarithm, positive definite matrix can reached. Use model$covmattransform='rawcorr' previous parameterisation. parameter used cells different default transforms, DRIFT diagonal -diagonal, now gives error. Previously cell transformed differently. New checks: ctReport() runs reporting checking functions fit saves results folder. ctIdentify() ctFitProfile() check identification julia backend, ctLaplaceCheck() ctParticleLik() check approximations julia fit makes, ctTracePlot() plots julia fit’s optimisation chains. New plots dynamics: ctNetwork(), ctNetworkPlot(), ctPhasePortrait(), ctStateDependencePlot() ctVarianceDecomposition(). title: ctsem 3.11.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-30 29/6/2026 Function names simplified remove Stan-specific wording main user-facing API. Use ctFit() rather ctStanFit(), new non-Stan helper names ctGenerateFromPriors(), ctGenerateFromFit(), ctPlotPosterior(), ctPostPredict(), ctSubjectPars(), ctTIpredEffects(), ctSummaryMatrices(). old names remain compatibility aliases existing code. See ctsem GitHub repository details: https://github.com/cdriveraus/ctsem. ctFit() now uses model model argument name. old ctstanmodel argument deprecated still accepted existing scripts. Modern fitting workflows generally use ctModel(type='ct') ctModel(type='dt') followed ctFit(). ctModel(type='omx') objects retained primarily data generation legacy workflows; convert ctModelConvertOMX() fitting modern ctsem format. System matrices can directly edited model object $matrices subobject, automatically update data.frame containing full specification $pars vice-versa. ctEmpiricalBayesFit new function fits single subjects specified model, computes empirical prior fits, re-fits subjects prior. Optimized-fit uncertainty can refreshed ctOptimUncertainty(), including Hessian, local surrogate, one-step bootstrap, full refit bootstrap, sandwich, outer product gradient approximations.
